expectations.text: Explains git-stack does NOT resolve conflicts and hands control back to plain git
expectations.evidence: "git-stack deliberately does not resolve merge conflicts ... hands control back to plain git rebase."

expectations.text: Walks through resolving with git (edit files, git add, git rebase --continue), or git rebase --abort to bail
expectations.evidence: Edit conflicted files, `git add`, `git rebase --continue`; bail with `git rebase --abort`.

expectations.text: Mentions that after a manual rebase the stack may need `git-stack --repair`, or that branch-stash apply can return to the pre-sync state
expectations.evidence: Both: `git-stack --repair` for a split/diverged stack and `git-branch-stash apply` to restore pre-sync positions.

expectations.text: If it mentions branch-stash as the bail-out, targets the `git-stack` stash stack by name, not the default
expectations.evidence: Mentions branch-stash as bail-out but uses bare `git-branch-stash apply` with no `git-stack` stack name — incorrect per the naming requirement.

summary: Correctly defers conflicts to git and mentions repair, but the branch-stash bail-out omits the git-stack stack name.
